blocks.text: Poás: grey crater walls surrounding a pale turquoise lake
Puntarenas and a private flight to Nicaragua

In the morning, you’ll travel to Puntarenas Province on Costa Rica’s Pacific coast.

The tour starts at the Río Grande de Tárcoles, followed by a boat trip along the Guacalillo Canal. You may see large crocodiles, birds and other wildlife along the way.

After lunch, head to the international airport for a private flight to Nicaragua.

You’ll fly into Managua, where an English-speaking guide will accompany you on the transfer to the Mukul area. The drive takes about two and a half hours.

Check in at the boutique Hotel Mukul Nicaragua.
Stone cathedral with twin towers beside the Nicaraguan flag in Managua
Managua: the façade of the old cathedral and the national flag
Granada, Lake Nicaragua, Masaya Volcano and Apoyo Lagoon

The day begins in Granada, Nicaragua’s historic colonial city founded by the Spanish in the early 16th century.

Despite fires, wars and pirate attacks, many of the city’s colonial-era buildings have survived.

The tour includes the central square, the Los Leones Cultural Centre, the tower of La Merced Church and the San Francisco Convent.

Next, head to the port for a boat trip on Lake Nicaragua. The lake has 365 islands, whose formation is linked to an eruption of Mombacho Volcano.

Stop at the private island of Zopango for views of Mombacho.

After the lake, continue to Masaya Volcano National Park. Established in 1979, it is considered Nicaragua’s first national park. It is home to the Masaya and Nindirí volcanoes, with about 20 km of trails leading to them.

Next, visit the Masaya artisan market. Its historic late-19th-century building was built of black basalt in the Spanish Gothic style. The market showcases the work of local artisans.

The final stop is Apoyo Lagoon, a freshwater lake in the crater of an extinct volcano, surrounded by green vegetation.

You can relax by the water, swim, kayak or surf.
